The dataset I select is: "NYC Restaurant Inspections"


I'm planning to do three graphs reflect relevant violation score x restaurant's association during period 2016.1.1-2019.2.1: 
1. A scatter plot reflects restaurant's geographic location and its cumulative violation score,
2. A boxplot showcases restaurant's cuisine type against the violation counts
3. A bar chart showcasesrestaurant's cuisine type against the total violation scores, if that restaurant only has one kind of score that day.



Step 0. Import
```{r setup, include=FALSE}
library(tidyverse)
library(p8105.datasets)
library(plotly)
library(flexdashboard)

data(rest_inspec)
```


Step 1. Data cleaning, defining my time range: 2016.1.1 - 2019.2.1
```{r define_inspection_period, include=FALSE}
inspection_period =
  rest_inspec |>
  mutate(inspection_date = as.Date(inspection_date)) |>
  filter(
    inspection_date >= as.Date("2016-01-01"),
    inspection_date < as.Date("2019-02-01")
  )
```

```{r inspection_summary, include=FALSE}
inspection_summary =
  inspection_period |>
  group_by(camis, inspection_date, inspection_type) |>
  summarize(
    n_violations = n_distinct(violation_code, na.rm = TRUE),
    n_scores = n_distinct(score, na.rm = TRUE),
    inspection_score = mean(score, na.rm = TRUE)
  ) |>
  ungroup()
```

Checking if the same restaurant, same day, same type of inspection will have score value more than one kind.
```{r check_inspection_scores, include=FALSE}
inspection_summary |>
  filter(n_scores > 1)
#There are seven restaurants have types of score more than one in a same day, investigating...

#Checking one of them, finding out there are 4 rows of score 15, and 5 rows of score 20.
inspection_period |>
  filter(
    camis == 40911114,
    inspection_date == as.Date("2017-11-04"),
    inspection_type == "Cycle Inspection / Initial Inspection"
  ) |>
  count(score, name = "n_rows")
```

Summarize each restaurant's cumulative violation score during period 2016.1.1-2019.2.1.
```{r restaurant_scores, include=FALSE}
restaurant_scores =
  inspection_summary |>
  filter(n_scores == 1) |>
  group_by(camis) |>
  summarize(total_score = sum(inspection_score))
#Keep inspection groups with one distinct nonmissing score (because I've screened out 7 times of restaurant with more than one nonmissing, distinct score at the same day)
```


```{r restaurant_data, include=FALSE}
restaurant_violations =
  inspection_summary |>
  group_by(camis) |>
  summarize(total_violations = sum(n_violations))

restaurant_info =
  inspection_period |>
  arrange(desc(inspection_date)) |>
  group_by(camis) |>
  slice(1) |>
  ungroup() |>
  select(camis, dba, cuisine_description, longitude, latitude)

restaurant_df =
  restaurant_violations |>
  left_join(restaurant_info, by = "camis") |>
  left_join(restaurant_scores, by = "camis")
```






Step 2. Making three plot

Column {data-width=550}
-----------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Recorded violations by restaurant location | Jan 2016–Jan 2019

Each inspection contributes once (no matter how many types had been checked at that day). Inspctions with missing or conflicting scores are excluded from the totals.
```{r violation_scatter, echo=FALSE}
restaurant_df |>
  filter(
    longitude >= -74.3, longitude <= -73.65,
    latitude >= 40.45, latitude <= 40.95
  ) |>
  mutate(
    label = str_c(
      dba, "<br>Cuisine: ", cuisine_description,
      "<br>Recorded violations: ", total_violations
    )
  ) |>
  plot_ly(
    x = ~longitude, y = ~latitude,
  type = "scatter", mode = "markers",
  text = ~label, hoverinfo = "text",
  marker = list(
    size = 4,
    opacity = 0.85,
    color = ~total_violations,
    colorscale = list(
      list(0,    "#16B9F5"),
      list(0.20, "#9252ED"),
      list(1,    "#F52E91")
    ),
    showscale = TRUE,
    colorbar = list(title = "Violations")
  )
)
```




Column {data-width=450}
-----------------------------------------------------------------------
#### Violations per restaurant by cuisine types

```{r cuisine_boxplot, echo=FALSE}
common_cuisines =
  restaurant_df |>
  filter(!is.na(cuisine_description)) |>
  count(cuisine_description, sort = TRUE)

restaurant_df |>
  filter(cuisine_description %in% common_cuisines$cuisine_description) |>
  mutate(cuisine = fct_reorder(cuisine_description, total_violations)) |>
plot_ly(
  x = ~total_violations, y = ~cuisine,
  type = "box", orientation = "h",
  color = ~cuisine,
  colors = colorRampPalette(
    c("#16B9F5", "#9252ED", "#F52E91")
  )(nrow(common_cuisines)),
  showlegend = FALSE
) |>
  layout(
    xaxis = list(title = "Recorded violations per restaurant"),
    yaxis = list(title = "", automargin = TRUE)
  )
#colorRampPalette is not taught in the class. I use this just to define my color scale. 
```

#### Cumulative inspection points by cuisine

```{r cuisine_barchart, echo=FALSE}
restaurant_df |>
  filter(!is.na(cuisine_description), !is.na(total_score)) |>
  group_by(cuisine_description) |>
  summarize(cumulative_score = sum(total_score)) |>
  arrange(desc(cumulative_score)) |>
  mutate(cuisine = fct_reorder(cuisine_description, cumulative_score)) |>
  plot_ly(
    x = ~ cumulative_score, y = ~ cuisine, 
    type = "bar", orientation = "h", 
    marker = list(
      color = ~ cumulative_score,
      colorscale = list(list(0, "#16B9F5"), list(0.5, "#9252ED"), list(1, "#F52E91")),
      showscale = FALSE
          )
    ) |>
  layout(
    xaxis = list(title = "Total recorded inspection points"),
    yaxis = list(title = "", automargin = TRUE)
  )
```
